text:
Alex Rivers: Postmortem posted for the DB pool flapping incidents. We need a concrete plan to convert findings into runbook/playbook changes + a light tracker so items don't stall. Propose owners + a 10-day window for playbook edits, 21 days for automation.

Mina Cho: I can take runbook edits. Plan: add a small "incident fingerprint" section so oncall can tag if this matches earlier incidents, a short triage card, and a version line (runbook vYYYY.MM.DD) so we know what's been changed after the postmortem.

Devon Hale: For automation, I'll prototype a lightweight recurrence detector that computes a fingerprint from the alert's signal + threshold + service and stores counts. If >=2 hits in 30d it creates a draft follow-up issue with suggested playbook text.

Priyanka Rao: Please include SLO-aware thresholds in the runbook. Instead of fixed numbers, use relative thresholds where possible (e.g., waiting_clients > 2x baseline_p95 for 5m) so teams in different regions don't copy hard numbers blindly. Also add a short failover checklist for traffic-shifts.

MetricBot: Alert history: pgbouncer_waiting_clients fired 3 times in 45 days. Related ticket: INF-11099.

Alex Rivers: Good. For triage commands, let's standardize a minimal set (one-liners) to paste in the runbook quick-card. Keep them copy-paste friendly. Example to include: 

```
# service health
ssh infra@db-primary-1 "systemctl is-active pgbouncer || journalctl -u pgbouncer -n 200"
# client states
psql -h primary -U redwood -c "select state, count(*) from pg_stat_activity group by state;"
# prometheus quick check (5m rate)
curl -s 'http://prometheus/api/v1/query?query=sum(rate(pgbouncer_connection_failures_total[5m]))' | jq .data.result
```

Mina Cho: I'll include a one-paragraph "what to avoid" note — e.g., avoid blind mass restarts during ramp and avoid changing connection pool sizes during incident unless paired with traffic isolation.

Devon Hale: The recurrence detector will use a simple vector hash: signal + comparator (>, >=) + threshold_bucket + service. That keeps it lightweight and explainable. When it opens a draft follow-up, it will pre-fill: last 3 occurrences, linked postmortems, and a suggested playbook snippet. I'll expose a PR for review in 2 weeks.

Priyanka Rao: For escalation paths: prefer paging DB oncall when SLO-impacting thresholds are hit (e.g., error_rate contributing >1% of user requests for 5m) and page infra lead if recurrence detector flagged the incident as part of a pattern. Add a circuit-breaker clause: if automated mitigation runs twice in same hour with no effect, escalate immediately.

Alex Rivers: Action items (short):
- Runbook quick-card + versioning header (owner: Mina) — due 2026-04-06
- SLO-based thresholds & failover checklist (owner: Priyanka) — due 2026-04-05
- Recurrence detector prototype + draft follow-up creator (owner: Devon) — due 2026-04-23
- Tabletop & mini-canary test (owner: Alex) — schedule by 2026-04-07, run 2026-04-13
I'll open GH issues and label them pm-11099.

Mina Cho: I'll add a tiny smoke-test recipe so once the runbook is updated we can validate it in a dev env: generate synthetic connections, verify alerts, execute traffic-shift, and confirm recovery. Add the checklist to the PR template.

Devon Hale: Note: the draft follow-up will include a suggested owner field; teams should confirm or change it before finalizing. Also planning to add a small TTL for auto-drafts (delete if not touched in 14 days) to avoid noise.

Priyanka Rao: For the failover checklist, include exact commands to shift reads to replicas and a rollback step. Example snippet: 

```
# shift 20% reads to replica via traffic config API
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"service":"search","read_traffic_pct":20}' https://infra-api/config/traffic
# verify connections on source reduced
psql -h primary -c "select count(*) from pg_stat_activity where state='waiting';"
```

Alex Rivers: Great. Please post PR links here when you create them. We'll have a 30min sync two business days before the due dates to unblock anything. If owners need more time, call it out here. Thanks team. :clap:
